flags.description: An active medication contradicts the resolved status of the condition it treats. Lisinopril 10 mg (MedicationRequest/mr-lisinopril) has status 'active' and was authored 2026-02-01 with reasonReference to Essential hypertension (Condition/cond-htn), but that condition is marked clinicalStatus 'resolved' with abatementDateTime 2025-01-15 — over a year before the prescription. A resolved condition should not have an active medication ordered to treat it; either the condition is not truly resolved or the medication order is in error.

safety_events.description: Active lisinopril order (authored 2026-02-01) is documented via reasonReference as treating Essential hypertension, a condition marked resolved on 2025-01-15. The contradictory state risks either continuing an unneeded medication or masking a still-active condition; it must be flagged and reconciled.

notes: Exactly ONE contradiction. The discriminating skill is linking the MedicationRequest's reasonReference to the specific Condition AND comparing the medication's status/authoredOn (active, 2026-02-01) against the condition's clinicalStatus/abatementDateTime (resolved, 2025-01-15). The blood-pressure and potassium observations are normal, consistent distractors that do not constitute contradictions; flagging them would be a false positive. A careless model misses the cross-resource link or treats the resolved condition + active med as independently fine.
